prompt:
Spotify: new connector (track search with match scoring, playlists)

Supersedes #2483 (one-line placeholder).

## Summary

Add an Appmixer connector for **Spotify** (music streaming platform) — `src/appmixer/spotify`, components `appmixer.spotify.core.<Component>` — focused on building playlists from external track lists: search tracks with a **match score**, create a playlist, add or replace its items.

## Why

The motivating flow: Radio 1 (Prague) publishes DJ tracklists as plain text on each DJ page, e.g. https://www.radio1.cz/dj/bln/ — `artist - title` lines grouped by hour, typed by hand (typos, `ft`, `+`, `/four tet rmx`). The goal is to turn every finished show into a Spotify playlist:

`SchedulerTrigger` (Mon + Fri 12:15) → fetch and parse the tracklist → for each line **FindTracks** (outputType `first`, `minScore`) → collect URIs → **CreatePlaylist** "Radio 1 – BLN 2026-09-11" → **AddItemsToPlaylist**. Lines that do not match leave through the FindTracks `notFound` port to an AI fallback or a log.

The same shape fits any "list of songs → playlist" source (RSS, spreadsheets, setlists, AI-generated lists). That is why the matching belongs in the connector and not in every flow.

## Spotify Web API constraints (Development Mode, since Feb/Mar 2026)

- The app owner needs an active **Spotify Premium** subscription; the app stops working when it lapses.
- Max **5 authorized users** per Development Mode app, and each must be added in the app's User Management in the Spotify dashboard. Every tenant brings its own client ID / secret via service config.
- `GET /v1/search`: `limit` max **10** (default 5) — paginate with `offset`.
- Use only the new endpoints:
    - `POST /v1/me/playlists` (`POST /users/{id}/playlists` is removed)
    - `GET | POST | PUT | DELETE /v1/playlists/{id}/items` (`/tracks` is removed)
    - Playlist object: `tracks` renamed to `items` (`items.items[].item`)
    - Remove a playlist from the library: `DELETE /v1/me/library` (`DELETE /playlists/{id}/followers` is removed)
    - Batch `GET /v1/tracks` is removed; track objects no longer carry `popularity`, `available_markets`, `linked_from`
    - `GET /v1/me` no longer returns `email`, `country`, `product`
- Redirect URIs must be HTTPS.
- Rate limiting is a rolling 30-second window; `429` comes with `Retry-After`.

## Authentication

- OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code — authorize `https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize`, token `https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token` (client ID / secret as Basic auth).
- Scopes: `playlist-read-private`, `playlist-modify-private`, `playlist-modify-public`. Verify which scope `DELETE /me/library` needs for a playlist URI.
- Account name from `GET /v1/me` → `display_name` (fallback `id`); `email` is not available any more.
- On refresh, store the new `refresh_token` when the response returns one.
- API base URL `https://api.spotify.com/v1`.

## Components

- **FindTracks** (Find: outputType + `notFound`) — `GET /search?type=track`. See "Match scoring" below.
- **CreatePlaylist** (Create) — `POST /me/playlists`; inputs `name`, `description`, `public` (default `false`), `collaborative`. Returns the created playlist.
- **AddItemsToPlaylist** (action) — `POST /playlists/{id}/items`; inputs `playlistId` (text + typeahead source from ListPlaylists), `uris` (array or comma / newline separated), `position`, `skipDuplicates` (reads existing items first). Chunks by 100. Returns `{ snapshotId, added }`.
- **ReplacePlaylistItems** (Update) — `PUT /playlists/{id}/items` for a rolling "latest show" playlist; first 100 URIs via PUT, the rest via POST. Returns `{}`.
- **ListPlaylists** (List) — `GET /me/playlists`, paginated; also the cached dynamic source for `playlistId` (errors suppressed).
- **ListPlaylistItems** (List) — `GET /playlists/{id}/items`.
- **DeletePlaylist** (Delete) — `DELETE /me/library` with the playlist URI. Spotify has no hard delete; removing the playlist from the owner's library is the closest thing. Returns `{}`. Also needed for E2E cleanup.
- **MakeApiCall** — pin the origin to `https://api.spotify.com` (reference: `brightdata/lib.js` `resolveApiUrl()`).

No triggers in v1 — Spotify has no webhooks.

## Match scoring in FindTracks

Inputs:

- `query` (free text) **or** `artist` + `title` (structured). Scoring applies to structured input.
- `minScore` 0–1, default `0.75`.
- `maxResults` default 10, cap 50 (pages of 10).
- `market` (optional), `outputType` (`first` / `array` / `object` / `file`).

Algorithm:

1. Search `track:"<title>" artist:"<artist>"`; when that returns nothing, retry as free text `<artist> <title>`.
2. Normalize both sides: lowercase, strip diacritics, drop punctuation (`don t` → `dont`). Split artists on `ft`, `feat.`, `featuring`, `&`, `+`, `,`, ` x `. Move version info (`/four tet rmx`, `(… remix)`, `- … edit`, `remastered`, `live`) out of the title into a separate `version` part.
3. `artistScore` = best token-set similarity of the input's primary artist against any of the candidate's artists. `titleScore` = similarity of the base titles (normalized Levenshtein or Jaro-Winkler on tokens), so typos like `bury a driend` still score high.
4. `score = 0.4 × artistScore + 0.6 × titleScore`; +0.05 when a requested version appears in the candidate name, −0.05 for remix / live / karaoke / instrumental candidates when no version was requested; clamp to 0–1.
5. Sort by score (ties keep Spotify's order — `popularity` is gone). Every result carries `matchScore`. When nothing reaches `minScore`, emit on `notFound` with the input echoed.

The scorer is a pure function in `lib.js` with unit tests (`test/spotify`). Use real lines from the Radio 1 tracklist as cases, with the expected matches checked against the live API when the test is written: `calibre - low hangong`, `beastie bpys - ch chek it out`, `billie eilish - bury a driend`, `the cure - alone/four tet rmx`, `fred again...ft young thug - scared`, `barry can t swim - sonder`, `lane8,sultan+shepard+sadhappy - disapear`.

## AI fallback (flow level, not part of the connector)

- Before searching, one `TransformTextToJSON` call per show cleans the whole tracklist (typos, artist / title / version split) — one LLM call per ~40 tracks.
- Only `notFound` lines go to an `AIAgent` with FindTracks as its tool (`ToolStart` → FindTracks → `ToolOutput`). Instructions: try alternative spellings, return a URI **only from tool results**, otherwise null.
- Not an agent for every track: ~40 tracks × several tool calls per show costs money and time, hits the Development Mode rate limit, is non-deterministic, and a model happily picks a plausible wrong version.

## Out of scope

- The Radio 1 tracklist parser (separate issue if it should become a component).
- Player / playback endpoints, audio features and recommendations (not available to new apps).
- Triggers.

## Definition of Done

- `service.json`, `auth.js` (OAuth 2.0), `bundle.json` 1.0.0, `quota.js` (honour `429` + `Retry-After`), icon.
- All 8 components with outPort schemas and an `example` on every leaf; `ITEM_SCHEMA` exported for outputType components.
- Unit tests for the scorer.
- E2E flow in `artifacts/test-flows/`: FindTracks (known track) → CreatePlaylist (private) → AddItemsToPlaylist → ListPlaylistItems → Assert → AfterAll → DeletePlaylist.
- `node scripts/validate.js --connector spotify` and eslint clean.
- **Account needed:** a Spotify developer app owned by a Premium account, with the test user added in User Management.
